objective: List every T3 Code setting (pingdotgg/t3code) with its key, scope, default and effect, and mark which ones matter for running HolyAgent on pi inside T3, so the maintainer can choose which ones holyagent setup writes.
scope: Sources: the T3 Code repository github.com/pingdotgg/t3code (docs/user/*.md such as project-settings, providers-pi, devices, html-renders, faq; the settings schema and defaults in the source, e.g. packages/contracts or apps/server settings schema, useSettings.ts, any settings.json schema), its releases and changelog, and the T3 docs site if one exists. Fetch with your web tools (for example the Exa fetch and search tools); use raw.githubusercontent.com or GitHub API URLs for source files.

For each setting: the UI location (Settings > ...), the settings.json key path if the source shows it, scope (server global, per environment, per project override, per device), type and default, and one line on what it does. Group by area (providers/Pi, approval and permissions, worktrees, git and PRs, terminal, browser and preview, devices, MCP and orchestration tools, scheduled tasks, notifications, models and effort, context and compaction, appearance, keybindings, other).

Then mark each as: relevant to HolyAgent on pi (say why: affects Full access, background specialists, worktrees, previews and the visual roles, device access, tool surface, pi provider launch, caching, notifications of completion), or not relevant. Background on HolyAgent's T3 plan: /home/user/holyagent-0.3.0/docs/pi/t3-code.md. Also answer: is hand-editing settings.json under T3CODE_HOME (~/.t3) supported or documented, and where is the settings schema defined (file path and commit)?

An earlier run of this research was lost to a restart; start fresh. Prefer raw.githubusercontent.com URLs for source files and the GitHub API (api.github.com/repos/pingdotgg/t3code/contents/...) to list directories.
constraints: Sourced facts only with URL per setting or group; label inference. The list is the deliverable and may run to 2000 words.

Relevance: each setting is marked relevant or not to HolyAgent on pi, with a reason for the relevant ones

SCOPE MODEL (S2, S1)
- Two stores. Server settings: `ServerSettings` in `settings.json` under `<T3CODE_HOME>/userdata/` (default `~/.t3/userdata/settings.json`), per environment. Client settings: `ClientSettings`, per device (appearance, confirmations, browser profiles).
- Per-project override: the 27 keys in `PROJECT_SCOPED_SERVER_SETTING_KEYS`, stored in `projectSettingsOverrides[projectId]`. Resolution order: project override, then environment, then `t3.json`, then built-in default (S2).
- Providers and diagnostics are per machine; a project can only switch a provider on or off (`projectSettingsOverrides[id].providerInstances[instance].enabled`).
- Home dir: `T3CODE_HOME` / `--home-dir` (earlier PRs called it base dir, `~/.t3` default). `service.env` under T3 home sets env for the background service (background-service.md).

SERVER SETTINGS (settings.json keys; defaults from S1). Rel = relevance to HolyAgent on pi.

Providers / Pi
- `providerInstances.<id>` = {driver, displayName?, accentColor?, environment?[{name,value,sensitive}], enabled?, config?}. Default {}. Pi driver default is DISABLED (S1 `DEFAULT_DISABLED_PROVIDER_DRIVERS` lists pi); Codex and Claude instances default on. Pi config (S4): `binaryPath` default "pi"; `launchArgs` default "" (extra args to `pi --mode rpc`; S3 says T3 rejects mode/session args and `--provider` needs `--model`). Effective enable rule: instance `enabled` false or config.enabled false disables, else `enabled ?? config.enabled ?? driver default`. Example write: `providerInstances.pi = {"driver":"pi","enabled":true}`. UI: Settings > Providers (S3). Scope: per machine. Rel: YES. Pi launch; the `environment` array can carry PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR or API-key env vars; `launchArgs` is the only Pi-side knob (HolyAgent plan sets none).
- `enableProviderUpdateChecks` true. Rel: no.
- `fallbackModelSelection` null (ModelSelection). Rel: no.
- `usageLimitSources`, `secretProviders`, `cursorKeychainUsageEnabled`, `usagePriceOverrides`, `usageModelAliases`, `usageModelFilter` (documented hand-edit, usage.md): usage/cost display. Rel: no.

Approval and permissions
- `defaultRuntimeMode` "full-access" (values approval-required | auto-accept-edits | auto | full-access; S5 and providerPolicy.ts; UI Settings > Threads > New threads > Permissions). Project-overridable. Per-thread mode is chosen in the composer. Pi: no "auto" (S3). Rel: YES. HolyAgent requires Full access for background specialists and extension tools; the default is already full-access, so setup need only verify or write it.
- Managed policy (`limits.maxRuntimeMode`, locked keys) can cap modes per machine (managed-policy.md). Rel: check only; a cap below full-access would break HolyAgent.

Worktrees
- `defaultThreadEnvMode` null (inherit `t3.json`, then local; values local/worktree per `ThreadEnvMode`, project-overridable). UI Settings > Threads (S2). Rel: YES, if HolyAgent wants new threads in worktrees; value names come from environment.ts, which I did not read.
- `newWorktreesStartFromOrigin` true (project-overridable). Rel: yes, minor (branch base).
- `worktreeSubmodules` null (recursive when null; "Top level only" / "Skip" in UI; project-overridable; `t3.json` `worktreeSubmodules`). Rel: maybe, for slow repos.
- `worktreesDirectory` "" (default `<T3CODE_HOME>/worktrees`; UI Settings > Worktrees > Worktree location; per machine). Rel: low. `previousWorktreesDirectories` is server-maintained.
- `branchNamingMode` "static", `branchNamePrefix` "t3" (UI says `t3/`), `branchNameInstructions` "" (UI Settings > Worktrees > Worktree branch naming; project-overridable). Rel: low, but HolyAgent branch rules (release/...) may want a custom mode. Worktree directories keep original names.
- `storageCleanup` {worktreeKeepWhen "uncommitted-changes", worktreeAfterDays null, worktreeSettledAfterDays null, worktreeOnMerge false, worktreeOnDelete false, worktreeUnchanged false, browserArtifactsAfterDays null, logsAfterDays null}; `worktreeCleanup` null (project-level {mode:"off"} or {mode:"custom",rules}; overrides storageCleanup rules). UI Settings > Worktrees > Cleanup. All off by default. Rel: low; note cleanup can delete ignored files and can remove worktrees of finished background work (inference).
- `addProjectBaseDirectory` "", `ghqCloneLayout` false. Rel: no.

Git and PRs
- `defaultAutoPull` false (project-overridable; `projectAutoPullOverrides` is the legacy per-project map). UI Source control. Rel: low.
- `pullRequestMergeMethod` null (project-overridable). Rel: low; HolyAgent uses `gh` itself.
- `sourceControlWritingStyle` {mode "repo_conventions", customInstructions "", followChangeRequestTemplates true}; `sourceControlWriterModelSelection` null; `textGenerationModelSelection` default codex model with reasoning effort; `threadTitleInstructions` ""; `removeAgentCreditsOnMerge` false; `reviewGuidesEnabled` false; `reviewGuideModelSelection` null; `reviewGuideInstructions` "". All project-overridable except `reviewGuidesEnabled`. Rel: YES for one point: `textGenerationModelSelection` defaults to Codex, so commit/PR/branch/title generation fails or bills the wrong provider on a Pi-only machine. Set it to a Pi model (shape: {instanceId, model, options}). Also relevant: `sourceControlWritingStyle` could keep T3 commit text compatible with HolyAgent's Conventional Commits and no-attribution rules (inference), and `removeAgentCreditsOnMerge`.
- `sourceControlHosts` {} (host config/tokens). Rel: no.
- `sidebarAutoSettleOnMerge` true, `sidebarAutoSettleAfterDays` 3, `sidebarAutoSettleKeepPullRequests` false (project-overridable). Rel: no.

Terminal
- No server or client settings key beyond `fontSizeTerminal`, `fontFamilyTerminal` (client). terminal.md: scrollback fixed 5,000 lines / 8 MiB. Rel: no.

Browser, preview, devices
- `enableAgentBrowserAccess` true (project-overridable; UI Settings > Browser; applies when an agent session next starts); `projectAgentBrowserAccessOverrides` {} legacy. Rel: YES. Gates the `preview_*` browser tools the visual specialists use. Keep true. Source says HolyAgent can't disable the bridge for Pi separately (issue #4150, no toggle).
- `enableAgentDeviceAccess` false (project-overridable; UI Settings > Devices > "Agents can use devices"; restart agent sessions after). `enableDeviceSupport` false (UI "Use devices"; does not grant agents control). `deviceOnboardingCompleted` false. `deviceHosts`, `easDeviceHosts`, `simlockDeviceHosts` [] and `simlockDeviceHostsEnabled` false (alpha). Rel: YES for visual roles on mobile projects: need both `enableDeviceSupport` and `enableAgentDeviceAccess` true, plus macOS/Xcode or Android SDK on the host; and ffmpeg for Android emulator video. Whether Pi reaches `device_*` is unverified by the sources.
- HTML renders (S7): no setting; "works with every provider". Headless browser downloads (~120 MB) on first preview. Rel: YES (html_render/html_preview are HolyAgent's visual route); no setting needed.

MCP and orchestration
- No settings key for the T3 MCP (`t3-code` server, `/mcp`), `delegate_task`, or tool toggles (S8, issue #4150). Outside-agent access is via UI "Copy MCP URL" (outside-agents.md). Rel: NO key exists; HolyAgent filters tools in Pi, as its plan says.
- `guestSharingEnabled` false (beta), `linkedEnvironmentsEnabled` false (beta). Rel: no.

Scheduled tasks
- Stored per environment through the UI (Settings > Scheduled tasks; webhook triggers with T3 Connect; S2). No settings.json key found in the schema. Rel: no (HolyAgent plan keeps this UI-only).

Notifications and background
- `snoozeLimitedThreads` false, `autoResumeLimitedThreads` false, `snoozePresets` (60m, 180m, today 18:00, tomorrow 09:00, monday 09:00). Rel: low (usage-limit resume).
- `continueThreadsAfterServerUpdate` true (project-overridable). Rel: low; relevant to long background work surviving updates.
- `responseStreamingMode` "paragraph" ("turn" | "paragraph"; project-overridable). Rel: no.
- `backgroundActivity` {schemaVersion 1, profile "balanced" (performance | battery-saver | custom), baseProfile, overrides{automaticGitFetchInterval, providerHealthRefreshInterval, hostPowerMonitor*Interval, pauseWhenHostLocked, pauseWhenHostLowPower, pauseWhenClientLowPower, pauseWhenOnBattery}}; legacy `automaticGitFetchInterval` 30 s, `providerHealthRefreshInterval` 5 min, `backgroundActivityProfile`. Rel: MAYBE. If the host locks or is on battery, `pauseWhen*` could pause work (exact effect on running agents not stated in sources I read); inference: "performance" or explicit pause overrides = false for unattended background specialists.
- Mobile push (S9): UI Settings > Notifications, needs T3 Connect and agent activity publishing. Rel: YES for "completion notices" to a phone; per-device, not in settings.json.

Models and effort
- `defaultModelSelection` null (project-overridable; UI Settings > Threads). Rel: yes, set to a Pi model so new threads start on Pi.
- `favorites`, `providerModelPreferences` (client-store merge; hiddenModels/modelOrder). Rel: no. Custom models: `customModels` inside each provider config. Pi discovers models itself (S3). Effort display: `effortDisplay` client.

Context and compaction
- `compactIdleThreads` (legacy) / `idleCompaction` (onReturn | beforeCacheExpires | off); default effective "onReturn" when absent. Documented for Claude only (HolyAgent plan notes Pi uses its own /compact). Rel: no for Pi. Claude-only `autoCompactWindow`.
- Client `contextWindowMeterEnabled` false (S3: Pi meter follows Pi usage). Rel: yes (useful, optional; UI see composer.md).

Speech/voice (`speechModelId`, `speechAcceleration`, `speechModelUnloadTimeout`, `speechProjectCustomWords`, `speechPostProcessingModelSelection`), `observability` {otlp*Url}, `environmentIcon`, `defaultTheme`, `defaultThemeSetAt`: Rel: no.

Internal bookkeeping: `projectSettingsOverrides`, `projectSettingsFolded`, `projectScriptOverrides`, `defaultProjectScripts` (project actions), `hiddenThreadTags`, `hideTaggedThreads`, `storageCleanup`: Rel: no.

CLIENT SETTINGS (per device; keys from ClientSettingsSchema; not server settings; storage is localStorage on web per useSettings.ts doc comment, and a `client-settings.json` in userdata per the third-party home-manager module; I did not confirm desktop storage in T3 source)
Relevant: `contextWindowMeterEnabled` false; `browserAutoShowFloatingPreview` true (UI Settings > Browser; "Auto-show floating preview"; agent browser/device floats over chat); `notificationMode` "off" (off | notifications | sound | notifications-and-sound) and `inAppNotificationsEnabled` false (completion alerts on the device); `followUpBehavior` "steer" (queue | steer; matters when a specialist's completion notice arrives mid-turn); `planModeEnabled` false; `toolCallVisibility` "showAll" (showAll | hideSuccessful | hideAll | zen); `showSkillsInSlashMenu` true (Pi skills in `$` menu).
Not relevant: `browserDefaultViewport`, `browserDefaultZoomFactor`, `browserDefaultAppearance`, `browserRecording*` (FrameRate, ShowKeyPresses, ShowMousePresses), `browserLinkTarget` "system", `browserSearchEngine` "duckduckgo", `browserCustomSearchUrl`, `browserProfiles`, `browserDefaultProfileId`, `confirmQuit` "hold", `confirmThreadArchive` false, `confirmThreadDelete` true, `confirmThreadUnpin` false, `diff*` (diffColorScheme "red-green", diffFilesCollapsed true, diffIgnoreWhitespace true, diffLayout "stacked"), `environmentIdentificationMode` "artwork", `glassOpacity` 80, `appearanceContrast` 100, `panelAnimationDurationMs` 0, `fontSize*` (Interface 16, Prompt 14, Code 13, Terminal 12), `fontFamily*`, `fontSmoothing`, `wordWrap`, `mathRenderingEnabled`, `chatWidth` "comfortable", `effortDisplay` "label", `composerRichTextEnabled`, `sendShortcut` "enter", `persistComposerContextStrip`, `proactivePanelsEnabled`, `timestampFormat` "locale", sidebar keys (`boringSidebarEnabled`, `boringSidebarMultilineRows`, `legacySidebarEnabled`, `sidebarWorkingShelfEnabled`, `sidebarProjectGroupingMode`, `sidebarProjectGroupingOverrides`, `sidebarProjectSortOrder`, `sidebarThreadSortOrder`), `threadDetails*`, `loadBalancingEnabled/Weights`, `pullRequestMergeMethodOverrides`, `pullRequestLinksOpenInApp`, voice/speech keys (`voice*`, `speech*`), `snapShot*`, `onboardingCompletedAt`, `favorites`, `providerModelPreferences`. Keybindings: separate `keybindings.json` in userdata (keybindings.md; home-manager module); not relevant.

PROJECT-LEVEL FILE `t3.json` (S2): repo-declared defaults for workspace of new threads, `worktreeSubmodules`, project actions, setup scripts; resolves below env settings. Rel: yes as an alternative to server-global writes: per-repo, no user-state edit (inference).

SETTINGS FILE QUESTIONS
1. Is hand-editing settings.json supported/documented? Partly.
 - Documented as editable: usage.md tells users to add `usageModelFilter` "to the server's `settings.json` in its `userdata` directory, such as `~/.t3/userdata/settings.json`" and says an invalid value is ignored and removed on the next save of any other setting; managed-policy.md says each policy key is a dot path in `settings.json` and "to find a path, change the setting in T3 Code and look in `settings.json` under `~/.t3/userdata`".
 - Code: serverSettings.ts header says it keeps "FileSystem.watch for concurrency and external edit detection"; the watcher loads external edits. Writes are sparse atomic writes (`stripDefaultServerSettings`). A maintainer comment on issue #18571 (2026-10-12) says "The server watches `settings.json` so that external edits are picked up" and that an unparseable file "must stay on disk for the user to repair".
 - Caveats (issue #18571, confirmed as a bug on main): a client save within ~100 ms of other saves can overwrite an external edit with the cached settings; an unparseable file is treated as defaults and the next save may overwrite it. Workaround: edit while no client is saving, then read back. Fields the schema rejects mostly decode to defaults or are dropped (hiddenThreadTags comment says bad entries drop alone "so a hand edit cannot reset settings").
 - Third-party precedent: home-manager's `programs.t3code` module writes `~/.t3/userdata/settings.json` (and `keybindings.json`, `client-settings.json`) and merges with jq; claude-mem's installer reads it. Not official.
 - Secrets: credentials are stored separately in `secrets/` under userdata and referenced, not inline (schema `settingsSecret`).
2. Where is the schema? `packages/contracts/src/settings.ts` (`ServerSettings`, `ServerSettingsPatch`, `ClientSettingsSchema`, `ProjectSettingsOverrides`, `PROJECT_SCOPED_SERVER_SETTING_KEYS`); Pi config in `packages/provider-pi/src/settings.ts`; provider instance envelope in `packages/contracts/src/providerInstance.ts`; file path derivation in `apps/server/src/config.ts` (`settingsPath = join(stateDir,"settings.json")`, `stateDir = <baseDir>/userdata`, or `<baseDir>/dev` in a dev server without explicit base dir); watcher/writer in `apps/server/src/serverSettings.ts`. Last commit touching settings.ts at read time: 4c3a9d58184f20bd76833bd599c3544d2c09e3eb (2026-11-07). There is no standalone JSON Schema file found; the schema is Effect Schema in TypeScript.

RECOMMENDED SET FOR `holyagent setup` (inference from the above)
Write (server settings.json, merged):
1. `providerInstances.pi` enabled (`{"driver":"pi","enabled":true}`; add `config.binaryPath` only when pi is not on PATH).
2. `defaultRuntimeMode: "full-access"` (default already; write explicitly only if a global/project value differs; it is project-overridable).
3. `enableAgentBrowserAccess: true` (default already).
4. `enableDeviceSupport: true` and `enableAgentDeviceAccess: true` only when the host has Xcode/Android SDK, since the default is false.
5. `textGenerationModelSelection` and `defaultModelSelection` pointing at a Pi model, if the user has no Codex.
6. Optionally `defaultThreadEnvMode` (worktree) per project, and `backgroundActivity` overrides if unattended runs matter.
Print as UI steps (client-side, per device, not in server settings.json): `contextWindowMeterEnabled`, `notificationMode`/`inAppNotificationsEnabled`, mobile push, `followUpBehavior`.
Check but not write: managed policy caps (`/etc/t3code/policy.json` etc.); restart agent sessions after browser/device access changes.
